V2.name: pong-vertical-control-v2
V2.guidance: Which action should vertically align the player paddle with the ball now? Read the objects with id player and ball in `observation.objects`. A bbox is [x, y, width, height]; its vertical center is y plus half its height. Larger y means LOWER on the screen. If the ball center is more than four pixels BELOW the player center, choose LEFT, which moves the paddle DOWN. If the ball center is more than four pixels ABOVE the player center, choose RIGHT, which moves the paddle UP. If the centers are within four pixels, choose NOOP to avoid moving past alignment. If the ball or player is absent, choose NOOP. The player being on the RIGHT side of the screen is not a reason to choose RIGHT. Likewise, a ball moving horizontally right does not imply that the paddle should move up. Judge the vertical gap, not the horizontal direction. Prefer the non-FIRE option when a FIRE alias would produce the same vertical movement. Act for only the next requested duration, then reconsider using the next observation.

A.name: pong-reflected-intercept-v1
A.guidance:
Which action should align the player paddle with the ball's expected arrival height? Read player and ball in observation.objects. Boxes are [x,y,width,height]; vertical center is y plus half the height. Larger y means LOWER. RIGHT moves UP; LEFT moves DOWN. If either object is absent, choose NOOP.
Use one target height. Normally use the ball's current vertical center. When valid ball velocity shows movement toward the right paddle (vx positive), and the ball's right edge is still left of the player's left edge, instead estimate its arrival height: divide the horizontal gap between those edges by vx to obtain raw frames until contact, then project the ball center vertically for that time using vy. Reflect the projected path at the top and bottom walls, approximately ball-center y=36 and y=194, including multiple bounces if needed. Reflection reverses vertical direction; do not simply clamp the projected height to a wall. Use this arrival height even if it lies opposite the ball's current vertical position relative to the paddle.
Use prediction only when velocity is valid and compatible with the latest history. A missing velocity is unknown, not zero. If recent history suggests a bounce has mixed directions within the velocity sample, fall back to current ball height until a consistent estimate is available. For a ball moving away, stationary horizontally, or already past the contact plane, also use current ball height.
Compare the target with the player's vertical center: target more than four pixels ABOVE means RIGHT; more than four pixels BELOW means LEFT; within four pixels means NOOP. Horizontal direction determines whether to predict, never which vertical action to take. Prefer non-FIRE actions over equivalent FIRE aliases. Recompute from the next observation after the requested four raw frames.

action_criteria.NOOP: Hold when the target height defined in guidance is within four pixels of the player's vertical center, or when player or ball is absent. For reliable incoming motion, compare against reflected arrival height; current alignment with the ball alone does not justify holding.
action_criteria.FIRE: A hold alias, appropriate under the same alignment or missing-object conditions as NOOP. It adds no vertical correction; prefer NOOP when their effects are equivalent.
action_criteria.RIGHT: Move UP when the target height is more than four pixels ABOVE the player's vertical center. Use reflected arrival height for reliable incoming motion and current ball height otherwise. A ball currently below the paddle can still require UP if its predicted arrival is above.
action_criteria.LEFT: Move DOWN when the target height is more than four pixels BELOW the player's vertical center. Use reflected arrival height for reliable incoming motion and current ball height otherwise. A ball currently above the paddle can still require DOWN if its predicted arrival is below.
action_criteria.RIGHTFIRE: An UP alias, appropriate when the guidance's target is more than four pixels above the player's vertical center, exactly as for RIGHT. Prefer RIGHT when the vertical effects are equivalent.
action_criteria.LEFTFIRE: A DOWN alias, appropriate when the guidance's target is more than four pixels below the player's vertical center, exactly as for LEFT. Prefer LEFT when the vertical effects are equivalent.

B.name: pong-incoming-four-frame-lead-v1
B.guidance:
Which action should align the player paddle with the ball's near-future height? Read player and ball in observation.objects. A bbox is [x, y, width, height]; vertical center is y + height/2. Larger y means lower. RIGHT moves UP; LEFT moves DOWN. If either object is absent, choose NOOP.
Use the current ball center as the default target. The principal change is a short predictive lead for incoming balls: when observation/history establishes reliable ball velocity toward the right-side player, target the ball center predicted four raw frames ahead. Express velocity per raw frame using the available history timing; do not treat an unknown velocity as zero. If the ball will reach the player's left face sooner, shorten the prediction to that contact time, using the horizontal gap from the ball's right edge and its rightward speed. Thus target height is current ball center plus vertical velocity times the prediction horizon.
For an outgoing ball or uncertain velocity, retain the current-height target. After a visible wall/paddle bounce or point reset, do not extrapolate pre-event velocity; use current height until post-event motion is established. Do not invent wall coordinates or extrapolate through a known impending wall collision without accounting for its reversal; use current height if that reversal cannot be resolved from the observation/history.
If target height is more than four pixels below player center, choose LEFT. If more than four pixels above, choose RIGHT. Otherwise choose NOOP. Horizontal direction determines whether to predict, never whether to move up or down. Prefer non-FIRE actions over their equivalent FIRE aliases. Act for the next requested duration, then reconsider.

action_criteria.NOOP: Choose when player or ball is absent, or when the selected target height is within four pixels of the player center. The target uses a short incoming-ball prediction only when reliable; otherwise it is the current ball center.
action_criteria.FIRE: Stationary alternative when both objects are present and the selected target is within four pixels of the player center. It gives no vertical correction; prefer NOOP under the supplied movement-equivalence rule.
action_criteria.RIGHT: Move UP when the selected target height is more than four pixels above the player center. Use the reliable incoming-ball prediction when available, otherwise current ball height. Prefer this over RIGHTFIRE.
action_criteria.LEFT: Move DOWN when the selected target height is more than four pixels below the player center. Use the reliable incoming-ball prediction when available, otherwise current ball height. Prefer this over LEFTFIRE.
action_criteria.RIGHTFIRE: Upward movement alias appropriate to the same target-above condition as RIGHT: the selected target is more than four pixels above player center. Prefer RIGHT when firing produces the same vertical movement.
action_criteria.LEFTFIRE: Downward movement alias appropriate to the same target-below condition as LEFT: the selected target is more than four pixels below player center. Prefer LEFT when firing produces the same vertical movement.
